title: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: MOE SkillsFuture adult learners
sections.summary: MOE has roped in SkillsFuture and tasked Institutions of Higher Learning with continued education and skills training for the adult workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: On changes gone right, the most significant move that the Ministry of Education (MOE) has made in recent years is its bold decision to rope in SkillsFuture and adopt developing the capabilities of adult learners under its belt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Institutions of Higher Learning (IHLs) are now chartered to embark on aggressive continued education and skills training for the adult workforce.

sections.label: 21st Century Competency Model
sections.summary: MOE's 21st Century Competency Model was developed more than a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The 21st Century Competency Model drawn up by MOE has been developed quite some time ago, more than a decade.

sections.label: EduSave and Meals programme
sections.summary: The money and meals provided in the EduSave and Meals programme in Budget 2018 are appreciated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The money and meals provided in the EduSave and Meals programme in Budget 2018 are appreciated.

sections.label: Device access for learners
sections.summary: A way must be found for learners of all socioeconomic backgrounds to access learning devices in schools up to IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As mobile devices become the gateways to learning, and Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) programmes allow students to use their own devices in a classroom, there must be found a way by which learners from all socioeconomic backgrounds have access to learning devices in schools up to IHLs.

sections.label: Teach to test, arts student
sections.summary: Teachers have learnt to teach to test, and a girl talented in singing and drama is taking an Electrical Engineering course at ITE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Teachers also have learnt to "teach to test".

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I know of a young girl who is talented in singing and speech and drama but who is taking an Electrical Engineering Course in the Institute of Education (ITE).

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: She achieved a score of 14 in her GCE Normal (Academic) level exams with 2As and 4Bs but only qualify for the Direct-Entry Scheme to Polytechnic Programme (DPP) which does not have any options in Performing or Creative Arts in the ITE or polytechnic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: She will spend her next two years in an engineering course in the hope that she can obtain a Higher-National ITE Certificate (NITEC) so that she can apply for Laselle or the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA).

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: She would have qualified, her mum says, if she had done better in her academics.

sections.label: PSLE as sacred cow
sections.summary: The PSLE is described as a sacred cow, a practice inherited for decades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One sacred cow is, of course, the PSLE, a practice we have inherited for decades.

sections.label: Singapore students top international rankings
sections.summary: Singaporean students consistently achieve top rankings in international benchmarking exercises such as PISA in Maths, Science and Reading.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Singaporean students consistently achieve top rankings in various international benchmarking exercises, such as the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) test in Maths, Science and Reading.

sections.label: Adjusting PSLE for Industry 4.0
sections.summary: Steps to adjust the PSLE, provide pathways, applied learning, internships and aptitude-based admissions are incremental, and Industry 4.0 requires faster, bolder action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Steps are being taken to adjust the PSLE system, provide multiple pathways and applied learning in schools, internships and aptitude-based admissions to IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, so far, steps taken are merely incremental.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With Industry 4.0, we need to move faster and bolder and continue to make education a strategic advantage to stay ahead globally.

sections.label: MOE steps for Industry 4.0
sections.summary: The passage asks what steps MOE is taking to transform education for Industry 4.0, noting approved operators, MOE Kindergartens and NIEC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to ask the Minister what steps MOE is taking to transform our education system to strongly position our future generations for Industry 4.0.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: More anchor operators and partner operators have been approved, MOE has come onboard preschool education with the setting up of MOE Kindergartens (MKs) and the Government is setting up the National Institute of Early Development (NIEC).

sections.label: Early childhood educator salaries
sections.summary: Salaries for early childhood educators must increase and be made comparable to professionals from other sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, salaries for early childhood educators must increase and be made comparable to that of professionals from other sectors.

sections.label: NIEC faculty from practitioners
sections.summary: Practical experience is equally important, and NIEC faculty should be appointed from senior experienced early childhood practitioners and sector academics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While theoretical and academic underpinnings are important, practical and grounded experience are equally important, if not more, particularly in dealing with young children and impressionable minds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would propose for faculty members of NIEC to be appointed from among senior and experienced early childhood practitioners as well as academics from the sector.

sections.label: Parents spending on tuition
sections.summary: A 2015 survey found seven in 10 parents sent children to tuition, spending $1.1 billion a year according to a 2014 survey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: A 2015 survey done jointly by The Straits Times and research company Nexus Link found a staggering seven in 10 parents of children from preschool to secondary levels sending them to tuition classes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: All in all, they spent $1.1 billion a year on tuition, according to the national Household Expenditure Survey released in 2014.

sections.label: Piaget and secondary school psychology
sections.summary: A speaker cites Piaget that children aged 11 and older can use logic, and urges the Ministry to study introducing psychology in secondary school Science.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to Jean Piaget, a world-renowned French psychologist, children between the ages of 11 and older, which he termed as the formational/operational stage, are able to use logic to solve problems, view the world around them and plan for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to urge the Ministry to consider conducting a study to assess the feasibility of introducing psychology in secondary school as a component of the Science subject.

sections.label: Students hearing non-ruling-party MPs
sections.summary: Students should hear first-hand from duly elected non-PAP MPs in schools on issues such as ageing society, public finance and social policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our students should be able to hear from and talk with MPs who are not from the ruling party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Students should be able to hear first-hand in their schools the perspectives of duly elected non-PAP MPs on issues of the day, be it our ageing society, public finance or social policies.

sections.label: Rules for MPs in schools
sections.summary: The same strictures on speech and behaviour should apply to both groups in schools, barring party canvassing, partisan discussion and party symbols, consistent with section 111.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The same strictures on speech and behaviour can be applied to both groups when they go into schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I believe that both groups should be allowed into schools but not to canvass for a party, not to engage in partisan discussion, not to wear party symbols and so on, that is, to be consistent with Education (Schools) Regulations, section 111.

sections.label: Confirming a 2011 change
sections.summary: The question asks MOE to confirm the change was made in 2011 and why it was made then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the MOE confirm that this change was, indeed, made in 2011 and why was this change made at that time?

sections.label: Joint registry of VWOs
sections.summary: The suggestion is to work with MSF on a joint registry of VWOs open to volunteers from the schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Maybe even work with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) to come up with a joint registry of VWOs which is open to volunteers from the schools.

sections.label: Terrex detention as case study
sections.summary: The detention of nine Terrex infantry vehicles by Hong Kong could be a case study on how Singapore could react in a crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For instance, the detention of nine Terrex infantry vehicles by the Hong Kong government could be used as a case study to reflect how Singapore could react in a crisis.

sections.label: Malay proficiency for students
sections.summary: Asks whether students who do not otherwise learn Malay in school can attain some basic proficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could we help those students who do not otherwise learn Malay in school attain some basic level of proficiency?

sections.label: Conversational Malay third language programme
sections.summary: Proposes making the conversational third language Malay programme part of the primary syllabus without examinations, and notes SkillsFuture does not cater to special needs students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It will also protect and preserve our multiculturalism and promote national integration and a sense of identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We currently have conversational third language programmes for Malay at the primary school level as enrichment, but not part of the regular curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As learning languages is best done when young, could the Ministry look into making the conversational third language programme part of the syllabus for our primary school students who do not otherwise learn our National Language, perhaps included as part of the regular curriculum for every primary school student, but without the pressure of examinations?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Many students with special needs fall off the cliff after completing their formal schooling at age 18 or 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Unlike their typical peers, SkillsFuture does not quite cater to them yet.

sections.label: Support for special needs learners
sections.summary: Asks how MCI and the Smart Nation Initiative supported the special needs community, and proposes a Lifelong Learning Masterplan for such learners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: How have the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) and the Smart Nation Initiative specifically supported the special needs community in terms of curriculum development, delivery and assessment and nurture both students and staff?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I propose a Lifelong Learning Masterplan be developed and implemented to empower and equip young and adult learners with special needs to be future-ready.

sections.label: Support for special needs students
sections.summary: Seeks the Minister's update on the existing, adequate and optimal support levels for special needs students in primary schools, secondary schools and IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: When I comb through online on what is available in Singapore and compare them to some of the other better models ‒ not all are better, but some are better ‒ there is a stark difference in the depth and quality, quantity of resources available to support learners with special needs in the mainstream classroom.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I, therefore, seek the Minister’s update on what is the existing support model, the adequacy level and the optimal support level that can be provided for students with special needs within (a) primary schools; (b) secondary schools; (c) IHLs, such as the ITEs, polytechnics and the universities.

sections.label: Enhancing SPED schools
sections.summary: Asks MOE to continue looking at enhancing SPED schools in Singapore's 4th Industrial Revolution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: The work of the CE Committee, I believe, is not over, and I ask MOE to continue to look at enhancing SPED schools in this 4th Industrial Revolution that Singapore is in.

sections.label: Assimilating special needs children
sections.summary: Notes EIPIC, FLAiR and DSP efforts to assimilate special needs children, and feedback that once-weekly DSP sessions are insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I applaud the efforts over the years to assimilate special needs children into mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We have the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC), Focused Language Assistance in Reading (FLAiR) programme for those who need additional help in English and Development Support Programme (DSP) to help mild to moderate special needs children to have a smoother transition to primary school.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: DSP educators gave feedback that once a week with the children is insufficient for those who need more intervention.

sections.label: Preschool anxiety and MOE study
sections.summary: A study found Singapore students have higher anxiety than the OECD average, and the speaker hopes MOE studies anxiety in younger children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When MOE rightly sought to improve preschool education by setting up MKs, some parents saw this as a new first stop to academic success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was reported that a study conducted by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) to look at the connection between well-being and PISA test achievement found that Singapore students have higher levels of anxiety, compared to the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, 76% of Singapore students reported feeling very anxious for a test even if they were well-prepared, compared to the OECD average of 55%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The students involved in the study were mostly Secondary 4 students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope MOE could do a study to see whether this kind of anxiety is also affecting primary school children and even children in preschool, so that we can learn how to mitigate the problem.

sections.label: Breadth of school sports
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Singapore schools have sufficient breadth in the variety and range of sports offered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Do schools in Singapore have sufficient breadth, in terms of the variety and range of sports offered?

sections.label: Central body for sports options
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a central body like the CCAB could administer and offer less popular sporting options not available in many schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Could, for example, a central body be set up, like the Co-Curricular Activities Branch (CCAB), which can then administer and offer sporting options which may not be quite so popular, quite so mainstream, and, therefore, not available in many of the schools?

sections.label: Nutritional health and meal costs
sections.summary: MOH and MOE are concerned about school children's nutritional health, and the passage asks how much students pay for healthy meals and whether low-income students can afford them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, in recent years, the Ministry of Health (MOH) and MOE have been concerned about the nutritional health of school children in two aspects, namely, healthier food and a balanced diet, to fight obesity and to get young people to adopt better eating habits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Also, how much more are students paying for these healthy meals on average and are we making sure students from low-income households can afford the meals?

sections.label: Survey on meal scheduling
sections.summary: The passage suggests MOE could survey all schools on meal and snack scheduling and provide an advisory for regular recess and lunch breaks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, MOE could reassure the public by conducting a survey of all schools on their meal and snack scheduling and provide an advisory for regular recess and lunch breaks to ensure students would never go hungry during the school day.

sections.label: Social mobility metrics and meal subsidies
sections.summary: The passage asks about resources and beneficiaries, notes the Government's two social mobility metrics, and mentions Budget 2018 meal subsidies for secondary students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How much resources are allocated to these schemes and how many beneficiaries are there per year?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, in reply to a 2013 Parliamentary Question (PQ) on measuring social mobility, the Government highlighted only two types of metrics: percentages of Singaporeans who did not complete secondary education as well as post-secondary education, and growth in the median gross monthly income from work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some governments, notably the United Kingdom (UK), have developed a dashboard of social mobility indicators based on a lifecycle framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The objective is to make life chances more equal at the critical points for social mobility, such as early childhood development, school readiness at age five, secondary school attainment, opportunities for tertiary education and getting into and on in the labour market.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: I am glad to see the announcement in Budget 2018 to cover more meals for secondary school students under the School Meals Programme.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Under the current scheme, primary school pupils receive subsidies of $2 per meal for seven times a week while secondary school students will receive subsidies of $2.50 a meal; $2.50 would seem insufficient for secondary school students.

sections.label: New PSLE scoring system
sections.summary: From 2021, the new PSLE scoring system will measure how well a student has learnt, not comparison to peers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For example, from 2021, the new PSLE scoring system will measure how well a student has learnt and not how he has done in comparison to his peers.

sections.label: PSLE kept as checkpoint
sections.summary: Effects of measures like Subject-Based Banding take time, but removing PSLE is not the way; PSLE remains a useful checkpoint.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: However, it will take time for the effects to be felt on the ground, including other policy measures like Subject-Based Banding, to increase the porosity in our schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: However, we do not think that removing PSLE is the way to go.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: PSLE remains a useful checkpoint at the end of primary school to help us determine where each child’s academic strengths lie.

sections.label: Removing PSLE shifts stress
sections.summary: Removing PSLE and having a through-train would transfer stress elsewhere, such as to Primary 1 registration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Removing PSLE and having a through-train will only transfer the stress on parents and students elsewhere, such as to the Primary 1 registration, where if I can paraphrase Ms Foo Mee Har in her words, it would then be a 10- to 15-year race to safeguard the child's interest.

sections.label: Subject-based Banding pathways
sections.summary: Multiple pathways to success are being created, and Subject-based Banding lets upper primary and secondary students take stronger subjects at a higher level.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Two, we are creating multiple pathways to success, something that Mr Low Thia Khiang mentioned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We introduced Subject-based Banding to allow upper primary and secondary school students to take subjects they are strong in, at a higher level.

sections.label: Changing academic results culture
sections.summary: Mr Low Thia Khiang asked that MOE complete its transformation by changing the entrenched culture of over-emphasising academic results.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Mr Low Thia Khiang asked that MOE complete our transformation by changing the "entrenched" culture of an over-emphasis on academic results.

sections.label: PISA and Israeli students
sections.summary: Using PISA as one indicator, Israeli students underperform the OECD average, while Singapore students outperform most peers regardless of socio-economic status.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: If we use PISA as one indicator, Israeli students underperform the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Here, we have high averages, where our students, regardless of socio-economic status, outperform most of their peers in different countries.

sections.label: Applied Learning Programmes in schools
sections.summary: Since 2013 schools have been encouraged to develop Applied Learning Programmes covering STEM, Languages, Humanities, Business, Entrepreneurship, Aesthetics and inter-disciplinary fields, now including STEAM.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Since 2013, we have encouraged schools to develop their own Applied Learning Programmes (ALPs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: It is a diverse, colourful and exciting landscape, catering to a wide range of interests: STEM, Languages, Humanities, Business, Entrepreneurship, Aesthetics, Inter-disciplinary Fields, and I will now include STEAM, as Ms Denise mentioned, to add "arts" to STEM.

sections.label: Primary school ALPs by 2023
sections.summary: MOE will build on the work done on ALPs and has directed all primary schools to set up ALPs by 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: MOE will build on the good work done on ALPs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: I have directed all primary schools to set up ALPs by 2023.

sections.label: New Science Centre for applied learning
sections.summary: MOE will set aside a significant budget to develop a new Science Centre, to be completed by the mid-2020s, providing applied learning experiences for all students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: MOE will make another major investment to prepare our children for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will put aside a significant budget to develop the new Science Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The new Science Centre will play a key role in providing such Applied Learning experiences for all students when it is completed by the mid-2020s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: It will bring science to life through immersive and interactive exhibits and experiences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: It will partner homegrown and international companies to provide a wide range of programmes to students and youth: hands-on maker workshops, experiments in specialised laboratories, opportunities for mentorship and research.

sections.label: NIEC early childhood programmes
sections.summary: NIEC will offer quality programmes to prepare those who aspire to join the Early Childhood sector with a foundation for a career as an EC professional.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Last year, the Government announced major plans to strengthen the preschool sector to give every child a good start and the best chance to succeed in life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: NIEC will offer a range of quality programmes to prepare those who aspire to join the Early Childhood (EC) sector with a good foundation for a career as an EC professional.

sections.label: Subsidised education and Student Learning Space
sections.summary: MOE is committed to quality and affordable education for all Singapore Citizens, and this year will roll out the Student Learning Space to all students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: MOE is also committed to providing quality and affordable education to all Singapore Citizens, regardless of their financial circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Our education today is heavily subsidised at all levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Ms Denise Phua mentioned Digital Equity, as learning is done more online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This year, we will be rolling out the Student Learning Space (SLS) to all students.

sections.label: Increase in Edusave contributions
sections.summary: Edusave contributions will be increased annually from 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Mr Edwin Tong and quite a few others in the Budget Debate asked about Edusave contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will increase the annual Edusave contributions from 2019.

sections.label: MOE FAS enhancements
sections.summary: MOE FAS will be enhanced with higher income criteria, larger pre-university bursaries and 10 meals for secondary students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will do more for students from lower-income families by enhancing the MOE FAS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will raise the income criteria for the Gross Household Income per month from $2,500 to $2,750, as well as the per capita household income per month from $625 to $690.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will increase the annual bursary quantum for pre-university students from $750 to $900.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will provide 10 meals for secondary school students under the School Meals Programme, an increase from the seven we provide currently.

sections.label: Cost and beneficiaries of schemes
sections.summary: The enhanced financial assistance schemes will cost close to $100 million yearly and benefit around 90,000 students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Overall, with these enhancements, the various financial assistance schemes will cost the Government close to $100 million per year, and benefit around 90,000 students in total.

sections.label: SEN students in mainstream schools
sections.summary: 80% of students with SEN are enrolled in mainstream schools today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Today, 80% of our students with SEN are enrolled in mainstream schools.

sections.label: Workforce preparation for SEN students
sections.summary: Students with SEN can join SG Enable's IHL Internship Programme and the RISE Mentoring scheme to prepare for work.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To prepare for entry into the workforce, students with SEN can participate in SG Enable's IHL Internship Programme, as well as the RISE Mentoring scheme.

sections.label: Scaling up S2W programme
sections.summary: The S2W programme has seen positive outcomes and is being scaled up with MSF and SG Enable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The S2W programme has seen positive outcomes, and we are working with MSF and SG Enable to scale it up.

sections.label: AED (LBS) provision targets
sections.summary: More AED (LBS) are being recruited, targeting two per primary school and at least one in 95% of secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: On top of that, there is at least one Allied Educator (AED) for Learning and Behavioural Support (LBS) looking at the behavioural needs rather than educational needs in every primary school.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We are recruiting more of these AED (LBS) and our target is to ensure all primary schools will have a baseline provision of two, and 95% of secondary schools will be given a baseline provision of at least one AED (LBS).

sections.label: Students discovering Singaporean identity
sections.summary: The passage states students must be empowered to discover what being Singaporean means to them personally, and that this was the basis for the NE Review Committee's work.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We must empower our students to discover what being Singaporean means to them personally − not because the syllabus or a textbook says so, but because they themselves know so through a process of discovery and the creation of a strong sense of their own identity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)

sections.label: Aptitude-based admission outcomes

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In addition, could the Minister also provide an update on the SkillsFuture Work Study degree programme: what has been the take-up rate for this programme?

sections.label: Germany vocational training coverage

sentences.text: In Germany, its vocational training programmes cater to 60% of the country's young people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Similarly, in Finland, more than 50% of the Finnish youths apply for technical and vocational education in training.

sentences.text: Similarly, NTU runs a College of Professional and Continuing Education, where alumni are entitled to 20% discount on courses.

sections.label: Singaporeans in SkillsFuture programmes

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: How many Singaporeans have taken up SkillsFuture programmes, such as Earn and Learn and the SkillsFuture Study Award since they were first launched?

sentences.text: SkillsFuture was launched four years ago at a cost of about $1 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Tharman said in a recent interview with The Straits Times that we are no more than one-third of the way.

sections.summary: The passage suggests the Government invest in training infrastructure for job opportunities, noting 42,000 new ICT professionals are needed over three years in finance, healthcare and logistics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: In the areas where there are significant job opportunities, I would like to suggest to the Government to invest and develop such training infrastructure to provide the economies of scale needed to develop strong capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: We know there are 42,000 new information and communications technology (ICT) professionals needed over the next three years in industries like finance, healthcare and logistics.

sections.label: Singapore ranked first in ICT skills
sections.summary: The PIAAC adult skills survey found Singapore ranked first among 34 economies for use of ICT skills at work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, the survey on adult skills conducted under the PIAAC study had found that among the 34 economies surveyed, Singapore ranked first for the use of ICT skills at work.

sections.summary: A study shows more variability in skills among Singapore workers than in other surveyed countries, with older workers performing poorer than younger ones.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, the same study shows much more variability in skills among Singapore workers than those in the other countries in the survey, with our older workers clearly performing poorer compared to their younger counterparts.

sections.label: NIR government revenue contribution
sections.summary: NIR contributed $15.9 billion to government revenues this year, exceeding FY2009's $7 billion, and is now the largest revenue source, much from GIC and Temasek Holdings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Much of the NIR, which is based on the national Reserves, has come from the Government Investment Corporation (GIC) and Temasek Holdings.

sections.label: Funding for post-graduate programmes

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, for some sectors, there is still considerable work needed to get the SkillsFuture and Continuing Education short-term skills-based courses up and running.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, would the Government consider delaying the decision to cut funding for post-graduate programmes until the ecosystem of short-term skills-based courses is more mature in those sectors?

sections.label: Foreign academics percentage decline

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Last year, the Minister in an earlier reply to me, mentioned that the percentage of foreign academics have declined from 47% 10 years ago to 40% today.

sections.label: PEI graduate employment survey findings
sections.summary: The first PEI graduate employment survey found six in 10 graduates found jobs within six months, earning $2,550, lower than autonomous university graduates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: In November last year, the findings of the first private education institution (PEI) graduate employment survey that was conducted by the Council for Private Education (CPE) and SkillsFuture SG was released.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: The survey found that six in 10 PEI graduates found jobs within six months of graduation, drawing an average starting salary of $2,550.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: This was found to be significantly lower than similar graduates from the AUs, such as NUS, NTU, the Singapore Management University (SMU), the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) or the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT), where, on average, eight in 10 found jobs within six months of graduation, drawing an average starting salary of $3,325.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Understandably, those from the PEIs have offered caution in simply accepting these findings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: There are still students who have spent large amounts of money on certificate, diploma or degree programmes offered by PEIs but have later on found that their employment options or career progression are limited due to a lack of recognition of their qualifications attained.

sections.label: Education changes and pathways
sections.summary: Education changes include revamping the PSLE scoring system, restoring DSA objectives, aptitude-based IHL placement, new universities, and work-learn pathways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For one, education needs to wear lighter academic colours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, we revamped the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) scoring system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Education also needs to recognise the diversity of strengths and talents amongst our young.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, we brought the Direct School Admission (DSA) system back to its original objectives, placed students into IHLs based on aptitudes and demonstrated interests rather than just grades alone, we started new applied and design universities, and we opened up work-learn pathways.

sections.label: SkillsFuture lifelong learning system
sections.summary: The system teaches people to learn and they never really graduate, which is the essence of SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In this system, you learn to learn, and you never really graduate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is the essence of SkillsFuture, and the most important feature we need to build into our system today.

sections.label: Adult learners in IHLs 2017
sections.summary: In 2017, 54,000 adult learners passed through IHLs, slightly over 10% of the adult learning market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In 2017 alone, 54,000 adult learners passed through our IHLs, slightly over 10% of the entire adult learning market.

sections.label: IHLs working with students longer

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The current approach will change when IHLs realise that they do not have three to four years to work with students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They have 20 or 30 years to work with students, because they will keep returning for more knowledge and skills after graduation.

sections.label: Earn and Learn and Work-Study programmes
sections.summary: There are 76 Earn and Learn Programmes training over 1,700 students, and AUs offer SkillsFuture Work-Study Degree Programmes with close to 90 students enrolled.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, we have 76 Earn and Learn Programmes training over 1,700 students so far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The AUs have also started offering SkillsFuture Work-Study Degree Programmes in areas, such as information security, business and analytics, software engineering, and finance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So far, close to 90 students have enrolled in such programmes.

sections.label: ITE Technical Diploma programmes demand

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: ITE received more than 300 applications for the 180 places available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Each course is at least 1.3 times, or 30%, oversubscribed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: ITE is engaging various industries and plans to roll out another 10 new ITE Technical Diploma programmes in the next two years.

sections.label: Polytechnics offering more CEPs

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Even an extra six months or one year is going to help.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Thus, from 2019, polytechnics will offer more CEPs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, all polytechnics already offer an Engineering CEP, and they will introduce two more CEPs – one in Business, and the second one in Information and Digital Technologies – two clusters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: From next year, we expect the two new CEPs to account for 30% of these cluster intakes.

sections.label: Polytechnics reducing courses

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Polytechnics will, therefore, reduce the number of courses by about 20% over the next two to three years, largely by streamlining and merging courses.

sections.label: Expanding programme to N level

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Given the success of the programme, we will expand it and extend it to students from the GCE "N" level stream with an aggregate score of 12 points and below.

sections.label: Aptitude-based admissions target for IHLs
sections.summary: The aptitude-based admissions target for IHLs was set at 15% of intake cohorts and will remain at 15% for now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, since young, I have loved art and I spent all my time doodling – and I meant really "all my time" and I used to have a lot of work to show for it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, last year, we set the aptitude-based admissions target for IHLs at 15% of their intake cohorts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The institutions have made good strides but they have not fully used the quota, so I will leave the target at 15% for now.

sections.label: ITE admission system review

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: ITE will embark on a review of its admission system, to rely more on assessing students’ aptitude through interviews and review of portfolios.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The revised system will be implemented in stages from the 2019 admissions cycle, starting with selected courses in the Business, Hospitality and ICT sectors.

sections.label: Increased funding for lifelong learning
sections.summary: By 2020, annual funding of IHL lifelong learning programmes is expected to increase by $100 million from about $210 million today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: By 2020, we expect to have increased the annual funding of IHL lifelong learning programmes by $100 million, up from about $210 million per year today.

sections.label: NUS Lifelong Learners programme

sentences.text: Last year, NUS announced that all alumni can take up two modules for free over a three-year period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Encouraged by the good response, NUS is expanding it into a programme called NUS Lifelong Learners, or L3.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Under L3, NUS will treat every student enrolment as lasting for 20 years, not just three or four years.

sections.label: Employers supporting curriculum and training
sections.summary: The passage calls for employers to help with curriculum, adjunct teaching, internships and in-house training, and to be recognised through the SkillsFuture Employer Award.

sentences.text: We need employers' hands on deck, too, to provide input on curriculum design, offer their experts as adjunct lecturers, place our students in meaningful internships, and participate actively in lifelong learning by providing inhouse training for their employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I agree with Dr Intan Mokhtar that we should give greater recognition to employers who support this, such as through the SkillsFuture Employer Award that was started last year.

sections.label: Fostering ingenuity for uncertain future
sections.summary: The passage states that systems built 40 years ago for identifiable challenges must now give way to fostering human ingenuity and resilience for an undiscernible future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, 40 years ago, we built systems to respond to challenges that we could identify.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We must now foster human ingenuity and resilience so that our children can thrive in a future we cannot yet discern.

sentences.text: (In Malay):   The Perkasa Warisan Camp is a collaboration between the grassroots leaders of the Malay Activity Executive Committee (MAEC) and our experienced teachers of the Anugerah Guru Arif Budiman Work Group (AGAB), with the support of the National Parks Board (NParks) and the Malay Language Learning and Promotion Committee (MLLPC).

sections.label: Perkasa Warisan camp pilot GRCs

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This camp will be piloted in Nee Soon Group Representation Constituency (GRC) and Tampines GRC this month.

sections.label: Wow Wild Learn Programme in Malay
sections.summary: After the Committee to Promote Chinese Language Learning and Wildlife Reserve Singapore partnership, the Wow Wild Learn Programme will be offered in Malay from August this year.

sentences.text: Following the successful partnership between the Committee to Promote Chinese Language Learning and Wildlife Reserve Singapore, I am glad to share that the Wow Wild Learn Programme, which turned the River Safari into a mega living classroom for our preschoolers, will be offered in Malay from August this year.

sections.label: Conversational Malay Programme and school programmes

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Today, 91% of our primary schools offer the Conversational Malay Programme or similar school-based programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Making it compulsory for all primary students may not be feasible with a number of competing demands on our students’ attention.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The current model, where the learning of a third language is encouraged but remains optional, is a balanced approach.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The school’s Learning for Life Programme is Environmental Education, and they partner an industry partner, Greenpac, which is a big advocate for green practices, to teach the students grow and harvest their own vegetables using a hydroponics system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The students benefited tremendously from this partnership as lifecycles of plants, a topic in the Primary 3 Science syllabus, came to life.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As their Values-In-Action project, the students further collaborated with the Residents’ Committee to share their harvest with the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: They also got the canteen vendors to cook the vegetables for the whole school to savour the vegetables of their labour during recess.

sections.label: Lifelong Mother Tongue Learning Courses

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)

sections.label: Professional capability in special education
sections.summary: The biggest challenge is deepening the capabilities of professionals in mainstream and SPED schools, not just having enough of them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The biggest single challenge actually is professional capability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, when we look at what we are doing now in our schools, the mainstream schools, the MOE-funded SPED schools, our VWO partners, the biggest single challenge is to not just have enough of the professionals but actually deepen the capabilities of those professionals.

sections.label: SPED Academy study
sections.summary: The SPED Academy will be seriously studied, with openness to improving and refreshing SPED delivery models.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: As to the SPED Academy, it is something that we will seriously study, we are quite open to improving and updating and refreshing how we do the different models of SPED delivery.

sections.label: Tuition expenditure and disadvantage
sections.summary: The Ministry's views on burgeoning tuition expenditure and how it disadvantages lower socio-economic background students were discussed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: In my cut, I talked about the Ministry's views or actions over the burgeoning expenditure on tuition and how I feel this disadvantages students of lower socio-economic background.

sections.label: MK places for lower-income children
sections.summary: In the MKs, one-third of places are reserved for children from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In the MKs, we reserve one-third of our places for children from the lower socio-economic backgrounds.

sections.label: Local and foreign faculty split
sections.summary: Faculty are about 50-50 local and foreign, while university leaders are about 70% Singaporeans and 30% foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, for faculty, both tenured and non-tenured, the split between local and foreign faculties is about 50-50.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If you look at university leaders – Deans and above – it is about 70% Singaporeans, 30% foreigners, quite in line with Minister Lim Swee Say's "two-thirds plus one-third, more than one".

sections.label: START programme for Singaporeans
sections.summary: Singaporeans doing meaningful local research are supported through the Singapore Teaching and Academic Research Talent (START) programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And they are Singaporeans, and they do meaningful local research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That is why we have the Singapore Teaching and Academic Research Talent (START) programme.

sections.label: School attendance and capacity
sections.summary: Anyone can attend the school, but the capacity in which one attends drives behaviour there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Anybody can attend the school; it has got to be a question of what capacity you attend in and that drives your behaviour in the school.

sections.label: MK special needs children progress
sections.summary: A question asks whether MK will take in and make more progress for mild to moderate special needs children.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Will MK be taking in and have more progress for mild to moderate special needs children?

sections.label: MK special needs support capability
sections.summary: MK has some nascent capability to support special needs children and will develop more support programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the short answer is yes, we have some capability to support special needs children in MK, but these are very nascent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: We will develop more support programmes and we will be building towards that.

sections.label: MOE curriculum and textbook review
sections.summary: Curriculum and textbooks are reviewed periodically in MOE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, yes, curriculum and textbooks are reviewed periodically in MOE.
